# Results — Study 810 (Price Delay)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Hou &
Moskowitz (2005): stocks into which market information diffuses **slowly** (high price
**delay**) earn a **return premium**, so a long-high-delay / short-low-delay book should
earn a positive spread. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number. Stamped as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the
partial current month is dropped; no partial months in the run). Fingerprint `357fd262912f`
(panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name, resampled to **861 weekly** (W-FRI) returns |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Market | equal-weight cross-sectional mean of the panel's weekly returns |
| Signal | each name's **trailing-52-week price delay** = `1 − R²(weekly return on contemporaneous market only) / R²(on contemporaneous market + 4 weekly lags)`, known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sort | each week rank the cross-section by the signal; **long the top 30%** (HIGH delay), **short the bottom 30%** (LOW delay), equal-weight; measure the week-`t` forward return of each book |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold week `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per **week** on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag) *t* on the weekly spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled high-vs-low books; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. Crucially,
the price-delay premium is documented as a **small, illiquid, low-analyst-coverage** effect; a
50-mega-cap survivor panel — names priced to the millisecond by thousands of eyes — is exactly
where it is *least* likely to appear, which is what we find.

## The headline — long-high-delay / short-low-delay spread

Weekly equal-weight top-30% minus bottom-30% price-delay spread (n = **804** weeks):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long high-delay − short low-delay)** | **+2.45 bps/week** |
| Newey-West(6) *t* | **+0.41** |
| one-sample *t* | +0.43 |
| high-delay book / low-delay book | +36.73 bps / +34.28 bps (Welch *t* = +0.20) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | +0.11 |

The claimed edge **fails to replicate.** The sign is *correct* — the slow (high-delay) names
did edge out the prompt (low-delay) ones by +2.45 bps/week — but the effect is **statistically
indistinguishable from zero** (NW *t* = +0.41). On a universe of 50 mega-caps, every one of
which is priced instantly by the whole market, there is essentially no dispersion in genuine
information-diffusion speed for the sort to monetise. The delay premium is a small /
illiquid-stock phenomenon that does not survive here.

## Placebo — is the (tiny) spread a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the delay sort but read each week's forward returns from a **column-permuted** panel
(signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **+2.45 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.057 bps (4.684) |
| right-tail p (observed ≥ permuted) | **p = 0.301** |

The observed spread sits barely half a placebo-σ from the permutation mean of zero — right in
the fat middle of the null distribution (p ≈ 0.30). The small positive number is what a coin
flip produces; there is no reliable signal.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=360) | +1.04 bps | **+0.17** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=443) | +3.75 bps | **+0.39** |

Flat in both halves — this is not an edge that hid in one era. Neither sub-sample approaches
significance.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per **week** on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/week | cost/week | net/week | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | +2.45 bps | 2.96 bps | **−0.51 bps** | −0.09 | −0.02 | −0.3%/yr |
| **5 bps** | +2.45 bps | 10.96 bps | **−8.51 bps** | −1.49 | −0.38 | −4.4%/yr |

The gross edge is smaller than a single weekly round-trip at a mere 1 bp one-way, so the net is
**negative from the first basis point**. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel where each name loads on the market with a name-specific lag; with
`knob>0` the high-delay names also earn a forward premium. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`knob = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.15** (sd 1.22), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** (the expected ~5% false-positive rate) |
| planted (`knob = 0.0018`, seed 810) | **+10.83** (Welch *t* = +1.79) |

The detector recovers a *planted* delay premium cleanly and fires on the null only at the
nominal rate — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine null on the mega-cap universe, not a
bug. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The famous Hou-Moskowitz price-delay premium does **not** replicate on
  50 liquid US mega-caps. The specified long-high-delay / short-low-delay spread is
  **+2.45 bps/week** (NW *t* = **+0.41**) — the right sign but a coin-flip, sitting at placebo
  p ≈ **0.30** and flat in both eras (*t* = +0.17 / +0.39), with a clean 20-seed synthetic
  control. The claimed edge is absent: delay is a small / illiquid / neglected-stock effect and
  mega-caps price the market instantly. *Survivorship: current-membership mega-caps —
  magnitudes are an upper bound, named on the Signal axis.*
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The tiny gross edge is smaller than one weekly round-trip; the book
  loses money net from the first basis point (−0.51 bps/week at 1 bp, −8.51 at 5 bps).
